title: Jonah and the Autopsy
premise: Sable Lockridge, coroner of the fading town of Marrow Creek, has spent three years burying her own past beneath meticulous paperwork. When a drowned man washes up wearing clothes stolen from her closet—clothes she never reported missing—she realizes someone is staging a murder that implicates her. As more bodies appear dressed in garments from her past life, Sable uncovers that the killer is her presumed-dead brother Jonah, who faked his death years ago and has been living inside the town's records, watching her. In the end, Sable lures Jonah to the morgue where their parents' bodies once lay, chooses duty over blood by turning him in, and finally claims her own name instead of hiding behind it.
about_author: Gideon Okafor is a former forensic technician turned novelist who spent six years in county morgues before trading the autopsy table for the writing desk. He lives quietly in the Pacific Northwest, where he still alphabetizes everything.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Sable performs a routine drowning autopsy on an unidentified man and freezes: he's wearing her gray wool coat, the one from her closet. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet dread cracking open a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter establishing Sable's three years in Marrow Creek, her friendships, and her habit of visiting graves. She reports nothing about the coat. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Missing Inventory
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dane Whitlock pushes for an ID; Sable stalls, then discovers two more items missing from her home—a scarf, a watch. She tells no one. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: A local woman, Ruth Ellery, claims she saw the dead man alive last week wearing 'that coroner's coat.' Her testimony contradicts itself in small ways. POV: alternating Sable and Ruth. Emotional beat: the town begins to whisper.

chapters.title: Fingerprints and Ghosts
chapters.summary: The victim's prints come back as JONAH LOCKRIDGE—Sable's brother, declared dead seven years ago. Sable destroys the printout. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What Drowned in 2016
chapters.summary: Extended flashback: young Sable testifying about the boating accident that killed Jonah—or seemed to—and the family secret it covered. POV: Sable (past). Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Second Body, Second Closet
chapters.summary: A retired teacher is found strangled, dressed in Sable's late mother's dress. The staging is precise, intimate, archival. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into pattern recognition.

chapters.title: The File That Reads You
chapters.summary: Dane notices the victims' case files contain details only Sable should know. He starts quietly investigating her. POV: Dane. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ruth's Revision
chapters.summary: Ruth recants her sighting, terrified. Sable finds a note in Ruth's mailbox written in handwriting she'd know anywhere: Jonah's. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: hope and terror entwined—her brother is alive.

chapters.title: Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable audits her own morgue records and finds pages altered in Jonah's hand—he's been inside her files for months. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: violation; her sanctuary was never safe.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Dane confronts Sable over dinner about inconsistencies. She lies badly; he lets her. POV: Dane. Emotional beat: two people circling truth neither can afford.

chapters.title: The Third Dressing
chapters.summary: A third body appears—dressed as SABLE herself, down to her boots. The town now openly wonders if the coroner is the killer. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: identity stripped away publicly.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: The state sends an investigator, Agent Priya Nair; Sable is suspended pending review. She keeps working from home. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: exile from the only identity she built.

chapters.title: Jonah, Alive
chapters.summary: Jonah contacts Sable directly—a phone call from a payphone, calm and loving, insisting he's protecting her from 'what Dad did.' POV: Sable. Emotional beat: love against every instinct.

chapters.title: The Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Digging into her father's old business records, Sable finds evidence he laundered money through the funeral home—and that Jonah took the fall before 'dying.' POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the family myth collapsing.

chapters.title: Agent Nair's Theory
chapters.summary: Priya lays out her profile: the killer isn't framing Sable out of malice but devotion—reconstructing her from her belongings. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: chilling empathy for a monster.

chapters.title: Ruth Ellery, Silenced
chapters.summary: Ruth is found dead, staged in Sable's graduation gown. Sable realizes each victim represents a witness to her old life. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Sable searches the family boathouse and finds Jonah's survival kit, newspaper clippings of her career, and photos taken through her windows. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: being known too completely.

chapters.title: Dane's Confession
chapters.summary: Dane admits he buried a report years ago at the father's request—the original cover-up. His guilt made him complicit. POV: Dane. Emotional beat: power's rot reaching even decent men.

chapters.title: Halfway Mark: The Alphabetized Town
chapters.summary: Midpoint pivot. Sable maps every staged body against town records and realizes Jonah is re-enacting their father's crimes in reverse order, oldest first. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread becoming clarity.

chapters.title: The Funeral Home Basement
chapters.summary: Sable breaks into the shuttered family funeral home and finds a room papered with her life—every report she ever filed, annotated in Jonah's hand. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the killer knows the file better than she does.

chapters.title: An Offer of Protection
chapters.summary: Jonah calls again: one name remains on his list before it's 'clean'—hers. He wants her to run away with him like when they were kids. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: temptation of surrender.

chapters.title: Priya Closes In
chapters.summary: Priya finds the funeral home room hours after Sable leaves it and suspects the coroner is either accomplice or bait. She offers Sable a deal: help trap him. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Set
chapters.summary: They stage Sable's 'flight'—a packed car, a leaked itinerary—to draw Jonah to the ferry dock. POV: multiple. Emotional beat: hope braided with fear of failure.

chapters.title: Wrong Ferry
chapters.summary: The trap fails; Jonah was watching them set it. Instead, Dane is found unconscious, dressed in their father's suit—the next 'character' in the reenactment. POV: Dane. Emotional beat: the hunter becomes the costume.

chapters.title: Hospital Vigil
chapters.summary: Sable keeps watch over comatose Dane, confronting what her silence cost everyone. Priya admits the case may be unwinnable conventionally. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: reckoning with complicity.

chapters.title: Reading the Killer's Margins
chapters.summary: Studying Jonah's annotations, Sable spots a pattern: he corrects her old mistakes. He doesn't want to destroy her—he wants to finish her education. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: The Last Unfiled Name
chapters.summary: Sable decodes the final entry in Jonah's sequence: it's dated tomorrow, and the location is the morgue. He's coming to her. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the end arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: Priya wants to storm the morgue with a tactical team; Sable argues it will get hostages killed. They compromise: Sable goes in wired, alone. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: trust extended across professional suspicion.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Sable waits alone among the drawers and stainless steel, remembering childhood games of hide-and-seek in this same building. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: stillness before rupture.

chapters.title: Jonah Comes Home
chapters.summary: Jonah appears—not threatening, but gentle, holding their mother's locket. He explains the murders as 'closing the ledger,' freeing her from the father's shadow. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: love and horror indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Autopsy of a Family
chapters.summary: Confrontation at its peak: Jonah opens the drawer holding their father's exhumed body and demands Sable perform one final autopsy—together, as children again. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the past laid open on the table.

chapters.title: Choice of Blood
chapters.summary: Sable picks up the scalpel—and instead cuts the locket cord, severing the symbol of their bond. She names him aloud as a killer, choosing duty over blood. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: identity claimed at last.

chapters.title: Steel and Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah shatters; the team floods in. He doesn't resist—only asks if she'll do his autopsy someday. He's taken away alive. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: anticlimax as mercy.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable testifies, telling the whole truth including her own concealments, sacrificing her reputation to end the cover-up culture that created Jonah. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: costly honesty.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Sable resigns as coroner, unable to separate the work from the wound. Dane wakes, forgives her, and confesses publicly too. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief beginning to breathe.

chapters.title: The Unmarked Grave
chapters.summary: Sable visits the empty grave that held Jonah's name for seven years and finally holds a real funeral—for the brother she lost long before the murders. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: mourning without denial.

chapters.title: New Ink
chapters.summary: Months later, Sable teaches forensics at a regional college. A student asks why she left the morgue; she answers honestly for the first time. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from truth.

chapters.title: Letters from Lockridge
chapters.summary: Prison letters arrive from Jonah—remorseful, lucid, still loving. Sable reads them all and answers exactly one, saying goodbye. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: love honored without obedience.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Final chapter mirrors the first: a new unidentified body arrives at her classroom lab, and Sable—no longer hiding—signs her full name to the report. The cycle ends where honesty begins. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
